title: SecOps-NG Vulnerabilities Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the vulnerabilities evidence stream (F-CP-04). One artifact is produced per (case_ref, execution_id) — one cycle of the F-WF-01 vulnerability-triage playbook over one inbound disclosure — and carries the triage decision plus the disclosure-timeline milestones the case has reached so far. Downstream consumers are the shipped KPIs `kpi.vuln_disclosure_sla@v1`, `kri.cvd_intake_aging@v1`, `kpi.patch_disseminated_on_time@v1`, and the four CRA-timing KPIs (`kpi.cra_early_warning_on_time@v1`, `kpi.cra_severe_incident_on_time@v1`, `kpi.cra_notification_72h_on_time@v1`, `kpi.cra_final_report_on_time@v1`). Public-bar artifact: operator-side strings (owner labels, advisory references) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped; individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<case_ref>|<execution_id>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipe). Deterministic on those two inputs so a replay of the same execution re-derives the same id and dedup is trivial.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

case_ref.description: Stable case identifier derived upstream by the F-WF-01 dedup primitive as the SHA-256 of `<cve_id>|<asset_ref>` (UTF-8). One case_ref groups every re-execution of the same disclosure across the lifecycle. Opaque 64-character lowercase hex digest.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Re-runs of the same case_ref produce distinct execution_ids — the regulator-notification chain treats re-emission as evidentiary signal rather than dedup waste.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (e.g. nis2:art-21-2-e, dora:art-9-vuln-mgmt, cra:annex-i-2-vuln-handling, cra:art-14-1, cra:art-14-3). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP-04 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses. At least one — typically `control.vuln_disclosure_intake@v1` and/or `control.sbom_capture@v1`.

triage_decision.description: Deterministic outputs of the F-WF-01 triage step. Free-text narrative for the disclosure stays in `risk_summary`; severity, dedup, CVSS, EPSS, and the CRA clock are typed.

severity.description: Final severity band after the F-WF-01 severity policy applies CVSS+EPSS+context. CVSS qualitative vocabulary so n8n / Temporal / LangGraph all consume one alphabet downstream.

cvss_severity.description: Unmodified CVSS qualitative band before context bumps applied. Carried so a reviewer can replay the policy decision.

cvss_base_score.description: CVSS base score in [0.0, 10.0]. Captured to 1 decimal place per the CVSS spec.

cvss_vector.description: CVSS vector string the base score was derived from (CVSS:3.1 / CVSS:4.0 prefix).

epss_probability.description: EPSS probability in [0.0, 1.0] at the time of triage.

actively_exploited.description: Operator-asserted indicator that the vulnerability is known to be actively exploited (KEV-equivalent flag). Pinned at triage time; the regulator-notification chain reads this to start the CRA Article 14(1) clock.

cra_clock.description: Which CRA Article 14 reporting clock was started by triage. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/cra_clock_kind.json.

dedup_outcome.description: Whether triage saw this case as new or as a duplicate of an open case. Drives whether the artifact opens a fresh disclosure_timeline or extends an existing one.

dedup_collided_with.description: When dedup_outcome is 'duplicate', the case_ref of the open case this disclosure was folded into. Omitted otherwise.

risk_summary.description: One-paragraph plain-language summary of the residual exposure remaining after triage. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names. Typically filled by a DSPy signature per the F-WF-01 narrative-summary precedent.

response.description: Response branch the triaged case was routed onto, plus the dissemination timestamp once the patch / advisory ships. Feeds `kpi.patch_disseminated_on_time@v1`.

band.description: Response branch picked by the F-WF-01 switch step. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/vuln_response_band.json.

case_opened_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the case was opened on the operator's intake queue. Reference point the per-severity dissemination SLA is measured against.

patch_disseminated_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the patch or advisory was dispatched to affected users. Omitted while the case is open. Required by `kpi.patch_disseminated_on_time@v1` once present.

advisory_ref.description: Stable identifier of the operator-side advisory or release the patch shipped under (CVE id, GHSA id, advisory URN, release tag). Free-text constrained to URN-shaped strings — no commentary, no commercial framing.

accept_rationale.description: When band is 'accept', the operator's rationale for accepting residual exposure (asset out of support, compensating controls referenced by control_refs, risk explicitly accepted by the owning role). Required when band == 'accept', omitted otherwise. Public-bar text: no individual names.

compensating_controls.description: Optional list of control stable-ids the operator is relying on to compensate for an accepted or scheduled case. Documentary for a reviewer; not consumed by the catalog KPIs directly.

disclosure_timeline.description: Ordered list of CVD / CRA regulator-notification milestones the case has reached. Empty array is valid — a triage_decision.cra_clock == 'none' case may carry no milestones yet. Each entry is read by the four CRA-timing KPIs to compute the on-time ratio against the milestone's declared deadline. Records are append-only across executions for the same case_ref.

milestone.description: Which CRA Article 14 milestone this entry records. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/cra_timing_milestone.json.

clock_started_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the clock for this milestone started — typically the operator's awareness timestamp on the case.

submitted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the notification or report was submitted to the competent authority (or the closest evidentiary equivalent).

submission_ref.description: Operator-side opaque reference for the submission (CSIRT ticket id, regulator portal receipt id, URN). Free-text constrained — no commentary.

on_time.description: Optional pre-computed on-time flag (clock_started_at + deadline ≥ submitted_at). The catalog KPIs may compute this themselves; the field reserves the shape for emitters that already track it.

reporter_acknowledgement.description: Reporter-acknowledgement event for the CVD intake. Feeds `kpi.vuln_disclosure_sla@v1` (acknowledgement-within-SLA ratio) and `kri.cvd_intake_aging@v1` (aging backlog count). Omitted when the case did not originate from a CVD intake (e.g. internal scanner finding).

disclosure_received_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the disclosure was first registered on the case ledger.

acknowledged_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the reporter acknowledgement was sent.

sla_duration.description: Operator's documented CVD acknowledgement SLA, ISO-8601 duration. Reference value `kpi.vuln_disclosure_sla@v1` reads to decide whether this case was on-time.

owner.description: Dated ownership pointer required by NIS2 Art. 21(2)(e) and DORA Art. 9(4)(a). Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'psirt@example.org', 'security-officer', 'product-security-wg'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of this case.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this artifact was captured. Stable input to the emitter's per-execution dedup decision; not part of artifact_id (which is derived from case_ref + execution_id so re-emissions in the same execution stay byte-identical).

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration, defaulted by the operator's configuration. Schema reserves the field; the default value is a community-input question (see docs/internal/f-cp-04-gap-inventory.md §4 q5).
